title.narrative: Critical winter support to war-affected Ukrainians

description.narrative: ltpgtThe war in Ukraine has led to the largest displacement in Europe since World War II. With ongoing hostilities, civilians are continuously exposed to indiscriminate attacks, severely impacting infrastructure and living conditions. Ukraine’s energy infrastructure crippled by continued aerial attacks, with over 60% of energy infrastructure not working, the coming winter is expected to be extraordinarily challenging for people. Given the extensive damage to energy infrastructure resulting from attacks by the Russian Federation, many households face rolling power outages and soaring energy prices. This situation is particularly dire in the front-line across the most affected oblasts (Kharkivska, Sumska, Donetska, Mykolaivska, Dnipropetrovska, Khersonska, Zaporizka, Odeska, and Chernihivska), where attacks continue to cause damage to homes and power infrastructure, adding to the already massive destruction. Local authorities in these oblasts have indicated that over 862,000 people are in need of winterization support. ltbrgtTo mitigate the risks of further displacement and enable people to stay safe and warm in their homes, UNHCR aims to implement a multi-faceted winter response. The proposed project provides critical support to 18,779 highly vulnerable IDP and other war-affected Ukrainians across the “crescent” who meet the established vulnerability-based eligibility criteria through cash assistance to cover winter energy needs, in line with the SNFI Cluster recommendations, ensuring they can stay warm and safe in their homes. This project aligns with the UHF 2024 First Reserve Allocation Strategy, which prioritizes winterization efforts to mitigate the harsh impacts of winter on vulnerable populations, and the proposed activity falls under the SNFI Cluster “Winter Objective 2: Heating to raise and maintain core body temperature”.ltbrgtPDM results from the previous winter have shown that cash assistance significantly improved beneficiaries' ability to manage winter-related expenses. The approach followed under this project empowers beneficiaries by giving them the flexibility to prioritize their needs, supports local markets, and aligns with the preference expressed by recipients in previous winterization responses. The transfer value of the cash assistance will be aligned to the SNFI Cluster’s guidelines ($525 per household). Vulnerabilities and capabilities specific to individual households will be applied to select the best assistance modalities based on beneficiary presence, vulnerabilities. When the cash assistance under the proposed project is not assessed as the best modality, UNHCR will provide other forms of winter support through it will implement with other funding sources.ltbrgtLessons learned from the 2023-2024 winterization response have underscored the importance of starting winter planning earlier in the year to allow for effective preparation and response. In this context, UNHCR has the capacity and systems in place across the country to immediately start its winterization programming, providing timely support, preventing further displacement and mitigating other protection risks, including through this proposed project.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented in close coordination with the Government and as part of the broader inter-agency Winterization Response Plan, particularly under the SNFI Cluster response led by UNHCR. Coordination with authorities and other partners, including under the SNFI Cluster at the national and sub-national levels, will be essential to reaching the most vulnerable efficiently. Local partners across Ukraine will be actively involved in outreach, verification and complaint and feedback management activities, and UNHCR will fully cover these activities that ensure the centrality of protection and AAP in the project through other funding sources. UNHCR will conduct the cash transfers through direct implementation.ltbrgtlt/pgt
